title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes.
journal: Cell, Sep 2026 (PMID 42727575; no PMCID; Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N). Preprint bioRxiv 10.64898/2025.12.04.692287 (Europe PMC PPR1232546, CC BY-NC). The Europe PMC preprint fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 and the bioRxiv JATS XML returned HTTP 429 (error 1015), so I worked from both abstracts plus the repositories.
data_url: https://github.com/hzi-bifo/Metax-analyses-figures (GPL-3.0; figure-source TSVs). Tool: https://github.com/hzi-bifo/Metax (AGPL-3.0). Raw benchmark reads: https://research.bifo.helmholtz-hzi.de/downloads/metax/benchmark_datasets/ (FASTQ only, not downloaded).

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the Metax-analyses-figures repo (9.2 MB tarball) and parsed all 41 TSV/CSV files with pandas. Key file: figure_4/marine_metax_truth_joined_profiles.tsv (1.57 MB). It has 14,446 rows x 15 columns: taxon, taxid, rank, reads, depth, abundance, breadth, exp_breadth, pvalue, chunk_breadth, truth_taxid, truth_taxon, truth_abundance, sample, presence. All rows are species rank across 10 CAMI II marine samples, with 3,190 TP and 11,256 FP. All 256 duplicate rows are in sample_9 (a one-to-many strain truth join). After dedupe there are 14,190 rows (2,934 TP) and abundance sums to ~100 per sample. There are 2,353 unique taxa, and 175 are TP in one sample but FP in another. pvalue is 1.0 in 14,100 rows. My single-feature AUROCs: chunk_breadth 0.968, breadth 0.963, reads 0.957, pvalue 0.514. A gradient-boosted model scores AUROC 0.970 / AUPRC 0.911 when grouped by taxid; with shuffled labels it scores 0.497. Metax's own per-sample species F1 is 0.862-0.885 (marine_opal_metrics.tsv, 20,250 rows, 19 tools plus the gold standard). Other files: clinical_ascites_csf_depth_genome_binned.tsv (22,248 rows, 6 profilers, 40 samples; Metax has only 555 TP / 9 FP / 5 FN final calls, with no breadth columns); marine genome reports (893 assemblies, TP/FP/BCO-FP); oral metadata (320 runs, 85 subjects; random-forest CV AUC 0.78-0.94 in oral_rf_roc_data.csv). The soil table has 2,784 rows (= 116 samples x 6 profilers x 4 ranks, matching the 116 sample dirs on the HZI server). The HZI benchmark directories hold FASTQ only (ascites/csf 80 files each; gut/soil anonymous_reads.fq.gz 1.7-2.5 GB). There are no truth files there, and the database is 35 GB.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstracts only: '>600 samples' (Cell) vs '>500' (preprint), the 55% higher F1 and 45% lower Bray-Curtis claims, and the peri-implantitis and plasma cell-free DNA findings. From the README/MANUAL only: that the marine table is Metax's pre-filter candidate list (inferred from 11,256 FP vs final ~40 FP per sample), and that the default chunk-breadth threshold was set on the CAMI HMP toy data. I did not read the methods or the discussion text, so the authors' named unsolved problems are not retrieved.

a1_downloadable.note: Pass (checked). The public GitHub repo downloads anonymously over the codeload tarball (HTTP 200), licence GPL-3.0. The raw reads on the HZI server are also open, but they are FASTQ and were not downloaded.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Pass (checked). The 'presence' column holds TP/FP per candidate taxon per sample, joined by the authors to the CAMI II gold standard. No other table offers a candidate-level label: the clinical tables carry only final calls.

a3_inputs_present.note: Pass (checked). Seven coverage features (reads, depth, abundance, breadth, exp_breadth, pvalue, chunk_breadth) are in the same rows. No sequences: any genome-level features would need taxid-to-assembly lookups for 2,353 taxa.

a4_units_stated.note: Pass (checked, minor). The README defines read count, depth of coverage, and breadth as a fraction. Abundance units are implied, but it sums to 100 per sample after dedupe, so it is a percent.

a5_enough_rows.note: Pass (checked). 14,190 deduped rows, a 2,934/11,256 classification. In disguise, though, it is 10 samples of one simulated marine community with 448 distinct true taxa.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Pass (checked). Trivial on CPU. Re-running Metax itself is not laptop-feasible: Linux x86-64 only, a 35 GB database, and FASTQ input.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Pass (checked). 10 marine samples is consistent with CAMI II marine. The supplementary README row counts match the files exactly (S2 2,784; S5 127; S6 46x71). The abstract sample totals differ (Cell '>600', preprint '>500') because the benchmark grew.

a8_label_provenance.note: Pass with flag. The label is the simulation gold standard, not a model output and not computed from the features. But it is synthetic (simulated reads from known genomes), so no physical measurement exists. pvalue is a Metax model output and is used only as a feature.

B1.why: One 14,446-row TSV holds the features and the TP/FP label together (checked).

B2.why: pandas parsed every repo TSV first try; no NA in the feature columns (checked).

B3.why: All labels come from one CAMI II gold standard via one join procedure (checked).

B4.why: Labels are binary with no censoring. Feature pvalue is saturated at 1.0 in 14,100 rows (checked).

B5.why: 256 duplicate sample_9 rows from the strain-level truth join; trivially deduped (checked).

B6.why: README schema lists the columns, but whether this is the pre-filter candidate list is undocumented (checked).

C1.why: Only interesting if it beats Metax thresholds; single-feature AUROC 0.968 already (checked).

C2.why: MAP2B random-forest false-positive filter trained on CAMI2 is open, but evaluated only on its own simulations (retrieved).

C3.why: Weak 'better' angle: a learned filter over hand-set thresholds, on one simulated community.

C4.why: False-positive filtering is already a cheap computational step inside every profiler.

C5.why: Metax per-sample species F1 0.862-0.885 published in marine_opal_metrics.tsv (checked).

D1.why: Inputs are seven tabular coverage statistics; no pretrained backbone matches this data type.

D2.why: No embeddings to cache; DNA models would need genome downloads for 2,353 taxa.

D3.why: No backbone; data repo GPL-3.0, Metax AGPL-3.0, fine for research (checked).

E1.why: Group by taxid (2,353 taxa) or by sample (10) is possible (checked).

E2.why: 10 samples and 2,353 taxa give enough held-out groups (checked).

E3.why: Majority class (78% FP) and a single chunk_breadth threshold are ready baselines (checked).

E4.why: Simulation truth carries no label noise and there are no replicates; the ceiling is feature overlap, not measurable.

E5.why: chunk_breadth alone gives AUROC 0.968; observed breadth tracks expected breadth for true taxa (checked).

E6.why: Shuffled-label gradient-boosted model collapsed to AUROC 0.497 (checked).

E7.why: No second candidate-level table with the same features; clinical tables hold final calls only (checked).

E8.why: Metax per-sample F1 in marine_opal_metrics.tsv can be recomputed from thresholded candidates (checked).

G1.why: NCBI taxonomy IDs present for every candidate and truth taxon (checked).

G2.why: NCBI RefSeq assembly reports, joinable on species_taxid; repo already joins 893 assemblies (checked).

G3.why: Species to assemblies is one-to-many (up to 10 per species in repo); needs a collapse rule (checked).

G4.why: Assembly-quality effect on false positives already shown descriptively in the paper's Figure 4b-c (checked).

H1.why: 11,256 false-positive and 2,934 true-positive candidates are both recorded (checked).

H2.why: One simulated marine community, one 2019 RefSeq database snapshot, one profiler's features (checked).

H3.why: The claim can be stated precisely; see honest_claim_h3.

H4.why: Simulation origin is explicit; the candidate-list status and the sample_9 join quirk are hidden.

I1.why: Profiler developers (the McHardy lab at HZI, CAMI) form a community, not a committed user.

I2.why: A learned filter would change one thresholding step, marginally.

I3.why: The decision is include or exclude a taxon; F1 and precision at a threshold match it.

I4.why: A single chunk_breadth threshold gives AUROC 0.968 vs 0.970 for the boosted model (checked).

J1.why: Tabular boosted-tree modelling with grouped CV only; no transfer learning or backbone.

J2.why: Coverage statistics are interpretable, but the metagenomics edge cases need a domain expert.

J3.why: A short note quantifying learned filter vs thresholds is the only shareable output.

J4.why: Implicitly a few days; no budget written.

existing_models.name: Metax (Deng, Safaei, McHardy; this paper; github hzi-bifo/Metax, AGPL-3.0)
existing_models.score_and_split: Statistical, not ML: breadth vs expected breadth plus a chunk-breadth threshold set on CAMI HMP toy data. Species F1 0.862-0.885 per sample on 10 CAMI II marine samples (checked in marine_opal_metrics.tsv). Gut mean F1 0.783 (0.909 with the 2025 database), checked.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Discussion not retrieved. The MANUAL says real-sample thresholds depend on read depth and on the long-read vs short-read basis.

existing_models.name: MAP2B (Sun et al., Nat Commun 2023, 10.1038/s41467-023-41099-8; github sunzhengCDNM/MAP2B)
existing_models.score_and_split: Random-forest false-positive recognition model on 4 log features (genome coverage, taxonomic count, sequence count, G-score), trained on CAMI2 simulations. Profiler F1 0.988 on its own simulations from random RefSeq/GTDB genomes; ATCC mock as a real check. There is no held-out environment or database split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Classification of species with no reference genome; mitigated via GTDB r202 (retrieved full text).

existing_models.name: GeCoCheck (Microbial Genomics 2026, 10.1099/mgen.0.001739; github R-Wright-1/GeCoCheck)
existing_models.score_and_split: Rule, not ML: keep Kraken taxa with 0.5% or more reference coverage. In simulations this removed 99.7% of false-positive taxa (abstract).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Real samples need depth-, biomass- and database-completeness-aware thresholds; marine and soil reads match only at higher ranks (abstract).

existing_models.name: BERTax (PNAS 2022, 10.1073/pnas.2122636119)
existing_models.score_and_split: Deep network for read-level taxonomic classification beyond sequence similarity. Different task (needs raw reads); title and listing only retrieved.

backbone.name: None fits. The inputs are seven coverage statistics; DNABERT-2 or Nucleotide Transformer would only apply after downloading reference genomes for 2,353 taxa.
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU for a boosted-tree baseline (seconds). Re-running Metax needs Linux x86-64 and a 35 GB database.
backbone.licence: Figure data GPL-3.0; Metax AGPL-3.0 (commercial licence on request); preprint CC BY-NC.

integration.partner_dataset: NCBI RefSeq assembly reports (assembly_summary_refseq; the repo already includes 893 TP/FP/BCO-FP assemblies with contig counts, assembly status and suppression flags).
integration.join_key: species_taxid (NCBI Taxonomy). One-to-many to assemblies (1-10 per species in the repo). Collapse rule: worst-case or median contig_count per species, using the 2019 CAMI RefSeq snapshot.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Are coverage-supported false positives explained by reference-database defects (fragmented or suppressed assemblies) rather than by the sample, so that a filter could flag bad references instead of bad calls?

controls.positive_control: chunk_breadth alone gives AUROC 0.968 (checked). True taxa should have breadth close to expected breadth. A trivial target (predict reads from depth x genome size) should be near-perfect.
controls.negative_control: Shuffled labels gave AUROC 0.497 (checked). Shuffle within sample, and ablate the chunk_breadth block to see whether the rest carries signal.
controls.external_validation: None at candidate level with the same features. The clinical ascites/CSF tables hold only final calls (555 TP / 9 FP) and no breadth. There is no year column.

honest_claim_h3: Among candidate species that Metax aligned reads to in 10 simulated CAMI II marine samples against a 2019 RefSeq database, a classifier on Metax's own coverage statistics separates gold-standard members from spurious hits about as well as a single chunk-breadth threshold. Nothing is said about real, host-dominated, or other-environment samples.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use how evenly sequencing reads cover each candidate microbe's genome to predict whether that microbe is truly in the sample or a false alarm.
plain_idea.train_on: 14,190 candidate species-in-sample rows (10 simulated ocean samples), each with read count, coverage depth, fraction of genome covered, expected fraction, and coverage-chunk spread.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the species was really in the simulated community (yes/no). The answer comes from the simulation's known recipe of genomes, not from a lab measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Profiling-tool developers could replace hand-set cutoffs with a learned filter. But a single cutoff already does nearly as well, so the likely lesson is that the cutoff suffices.

ml_idea: Gradient-boosted or logistic classifier on the 7 coverage features, with leave-taxon-out and leave-sample-out CV, compared against a single chunk_breadth threshold and Metax's reported F1. An optional add-on is RefSeq assembly-quality features joined on species_taxid. It was already tried here: boosted model AUROC 0.970 vs threshold 0.968.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: on the deduped marine table, compare a grouped-CV boosted model with the best single chunk_breadth threshold. It gave AUROC 0.970 vs 0.968 and AUPRC 0.911 vs 0.875, so the ML gain is marginal. That check kills the project unless the gain holds on a second, non-marine candidate table, which does not exist in the release.

verdict_reason: Part A passes on a clean 14,190-row candidate table (one simulated marine community, TP/FP from the CAMI gold standard), but the question isn't worth a project. A single coverage threshold already matches a boosted model (AUROC 0.968 vs 0.970), no backbone fits, MAP2B already ships an open random-forest false-positive filter, and any transfer test needs Metax re-run on raw FASTQ (Linux-only, 35 GB database). The oral cohort is 320 runs from 85 subjects, under A5.
